# More model features: when to use each, and how it is stored

This file covers model features that the other files beside it leave out: extra partitions, more storage forms, model-wide switches, and the files of a model folder that no instruction names.
For each one it says when Microsoft says to use it, its release status, the limits Microsoft lists, the exact keywords in the files, the shipped example to copy (or why there is none), and what the check reads.
All example paths below start at `tests/fixtures/examples/`. Nothing there has been opened in Power BI Desktop, and Microsoft's library, which wrote the files, does not parse DAX or Power Query: look at the first use of each kind in Desktop.

A preview feature is used only after the developer's yes, recorded in section 11 of `docs/report-brief.md`. Source: `.github/skills/pbi-semantic-model/SKILL.md` ("A better native feature").

## A. Partitions and storage

**1. Several partitions on one table.** For a very large table whose parts load or refresh apart from each other. Power BI Desktop does not show partitions; incremental refresh makes them for you, and anything beyond that is done through the XMLA endpoint. Status: no preview label. Limits: a table holds at most one DirectQuery partition (a hybrid table: import partitions plus one DirectQuery partition); partitions must not overlap, because the engine does not check it. Stored as one `partition '<Name>' = m` block per partition, each with its own `mode:` and `source =`, inside one table. Example: `storage/Hybrid.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Sales History.tmdl` ('Sales History Recent' and 'Sales History Older'). Check: M117 warns only when a table has one partition with a name other than the table's. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tom/table-partitions ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tabular-models/define-partitions-in-directquery-models-ssas-tabular

**2. Hybrid table (incremental refresh with real-time data).** For a fact table that needs the newest rows at once while the older rows stay imported. Status: GA. Limits: Premium, Premium Per User or Embedded only, never Pro; every partition reads one source; no transformation that does not fold; tables related to it should be Dual; after the first publish, publishing again from Desktop drops the partitions and their data. Stored as `refreshPolicy` with `mode: hybrid` on top of the usual policy lines; the service then adds the DirectQuery partition. Example: `storage/Hybrid.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Sales.tmdl`, with `Date` in Dual mode beside it. An aggregation table cannot sit on a hybrid table (the file `storage-and-security.md` beside this one, rule 25). Checks: M707 and M709, as for any refresh policy. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/incremental-refresh-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/incremental-refresh-xmla

**3. Data coverage definition.** For a table with an import partition for recent data and a DirectQuery partition for old data: it tells the engine which rows the DirectQuery partition holds, so queries on recent data skip the source. Status: no preview label; compatibility level 1603 or higher. Limits Microsoft lists: fixed values only, never `TODAY ()` and the like; a dimension named through RELATED must be in Dual mode; a wrong definition gives wrong numbers, so compare results with and without it; refresh after each change; a hybrid policy drops the definition when it remakes its DirectQuery partition. Stored under the DirectQuery partition, after its source: `dataCoverageDefinition = RELATED ( 'Date'[Year] ) IN { 2022, 2023 }`. Example: the partition 'Sales History Older' in `storage/Hybrid.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Sales History.tmdl`. It has no `///` line of its own: the check reads one there as a description above no object (D003). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tom/table-partitions ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.datacoveragedefinition

**4. Direct Lake on SQL or on OneLake.** Microsoft's split, restated:
- On OneLake when the data comes from one or more Fabric items, when the model mixes in Import or DirectQuery tables, when OneLake security is used, or when the model needs calculated columns or tables over Direct Lake data (preview). It never falls back to DirectQuery.
- On SQL when security rules live in the SQL analytics endpoint, or when tables are SQL views. It can fall back to DirectQuery; the model property `directLakeBehavior` decides: `automatic` (the default, written by leaving the line out), `directLakeOnly` (a query fails instead, for development), `directQueryOnly` (for measuring fallback). Microsoft advises the default in production.
- How each is stored: Direct Lake on OneLake points its shared expression at `AzureStorage.DataLake` with the workspace and item IDs (`storage/DirectLake.SemanticModel/definition/expressions.tmdl`). Direct Lake on SQL points it at `Sql.Database` with the endpoint and the endpoint's ID, never its friendly name (`storage/DirectLakeSql.SemanticModel/definition/expressions.tmdl`, expression `DatabaseQuery`, and `directLakeBehavior: directLakeOnly` in its `model.tmdl`). Both use `partition <Name> = entity` with `mode: directLake`, `entityName`, `schemaName` and `expressionSource`.
- Fabric SQL databases, mirrored databases and mirrored catalogs use the same two forms; for a warehouse the OneLake form takes a warehouse ID instead of a lakehouse ID. No separate example.
- Status: GA. Limits: the file `storage-and-security.md` beside this one, rule 27. No check. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/direct-lake-develop ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/direct-lake-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/direct-lake-how-it-works ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/articles/item-management/definitions/ontology-definition

**5. Direct Lake on OneLake plus Import tables.** For a model whose large facts stay in OneLake while a small table comes from any other source. Status: the Learn pages read carry no preview label; this template's inventory recorded it as preview, so the example sits under `preview/`. Limits: Direct Lake on SQL cannot mix; import tables are added in web modeling, not in Desktop; relationships between the two kinds are regular. Stored as an ordinary import table (`partition ... = m`, `mode: import`) next to entity partitions. Example: `preview/DirectLakeComposite.SemanticModel` (Date is imported; Sales and Store are Direct Lake). No check. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/direct-lake-web-modeling ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-composite-models

**6. Calculated table over Direct Lake data (preview).** For a small summary that the lakehouse cannot provide. Prefer making it in the lakehouse. Limits: Direct Lake on OneLake only; on SQL only calculation groups and parameter tables are allowed. Stored as `partition ... = calculated` that names a Direct Lake table, with `annotation CalculatedReason`. Example: `preview/DirectLakeComposite.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Daily Sales.tmdl`. Check: M105 (fail) for the reason line. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/direct-lake-overview

**7. User-context calculated column (preview).** For a column whose value depends on the reader, through USERCULTURE, USERPRINCIPALNAME, USEROBJECTID, USERNAME or CUSTOMDATA, such as names in the reader's language. Limits: worked out at query time and never stored, so it is slower and cannot carry a relationship; in Direct Lake on OneLake it is the only kind of calculated column (preview); Direct Lake on SQL has none. Stored as `expressionContext: userContext` under the calculated column; Microsoft's library requires compatibility level 1705. Example: 'Store Name Local' in `preview/DirectLakeComposite.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Store.tmdl`. Check: M105 (fail) for the reason line. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-calculated-columns ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.calculatedcolumn.expressioncontext

**8. Composite model on a published model, and EXTERNALMEASURE.** For extending a published semantic model or an Analysis Services model with your own tables. Status: GA. Limits: the remote model is in the same tenant; tenant switches must allow it; security on the source model is not copied; keep relationship keys across sources small. EXTERNALMEASURE calls a measure of the remote model by name, with a type and the connection name, and works only in such a model. Not built: Microsoft Learn gives no file form for the remote connection or its tables. Build it in Power BI Desktop (Make changes to this model); afterwards copy only from that model's own files. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-composite-models ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/externalmeasure-function-dax

**9. Dynamic M query parameter.** For a DirectQuery source where the reader's pick in a slicer must reach the source query at a set place. Status: no preview label. Limits: one parameter per column and the other way round; no aggregations; no row-level security; the parameter name has no spaces and is no DAX reserved word; the column's type matches the parameter's; many filter kinds do not pass the value. Microsoft warns that joining the value into query text opens the source to injection: filter with a step that folds instead. Stored as `parameterValuesColumn: '<Table>'.'<Column>'` under the parameter `expression`, plus a table of values with no relationship. Example: `storage/DynamicParameter.SemanticModel` (RegionParameter, table 'Region Choice', Sales). The table of values gives M411 (warn) on purpose; list it in section 9 of the brief with its reason. Multi-select and Select all are switched on in Desktop; their stored form is not given. P002 warns on a native query made by joining text. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-dynamic-m-query-parameters ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.namedexpression.parametervaluescolumn

**10. Python or R script as a data source.** It runs code on the developer's own machine at every refresh. Copilot does not write one; it may describe the option. Limits: Python and R are installed locally; a script stops after 30 minutes; nested tables fail (Python); every source in the query must have the privacy level Public; refresh in the service needs a personal gateway on the machine that holds the file and the language. Not built: guidance only. No check. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-python-scripts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-python-in-query-editor ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-r-scripts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-r-in-query-editor

## B. Columns and calculation groups

**11. Barcode.** For a column of product barcodes that the Power BI mobile app scans to filter a report. Status: no preview label. Limits: one barcode column in all tables of a report, or no filter happens; Microsoft lists the barcode formats it reads. Stored as `dataCategory: Barcode` on a text column. Example: Product[Barcode] in `Examples.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Product.tmdl`. Check: none (M114 reads place names only). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-mobile-barcodes

**12. Groups and bins.** For putting values in a few named groups, or numbers and dates in bins of equal size. A bin works on a column, not on a measure. Not built: Learn shows only the Desktop dialog (New group) and not how a group is stored. Make it in Desktop, or write a calculated column with SWITCH and its reason line. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-grouping-and-binning

**13. Selection expressions of a calculation group.** For what a group returns when readers pick two or more items, or none that exists (`multipleOrEmptySelectionExpression`), or nothing at all (`noSelectionExpression`). Each may carry its own `formatStringDefinition`. Without them the group acts as if unfiltered. The model property `selectionExpressionBehavior` (`automatic`, `nonVisual`, `visual`) sets what happens when they are missing; `automatic` behaves as `nonVisual` today. Status: no preview label; level 1605 for the expressions, 1609 for the property. Stored inside `calculationGroup`, below `precedence`. Example: `Examples.SemanticModel/definition/tables/Time Calculation.tmdl` (blank for several picks, the plain measure for none) and `selectionExpressionBehavior: nonVisual` in `Examples.SemanticModel/definition/model.tmdl`. The expressions carry no `///` line (D003, as in rule 3). Check: none on the expressions. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tabular-models/calculation-groups ("Selection expressions")

**14. Detail rows and calculation groups.** Microsoft states that detail rows expressions do not work in a model with a calculation group. The shipped `Examples.SemanticModel` holds both (`# Order Lines` and 'Time Calculation') only to show each form. A real model picks one: ask the developer which. No check yet. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/analysis-services/tabular-models/calculation-groups ("Limitations")

## C. Model-wide switches

**15. Discourage composite models.** For a published model that no one should extend with DirectQuery, so that chains of models stop. Power BI honours it; other tools may not. Set in Desktop under Options, Current File, Published semantic model settings. Stored as the bare flag `discourageCompositeModels` in `model.tmdl`. Status: no preview label. Example: `storage/ModelOptions.SemanticModel/definition/model.tmdl`. No check. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-discourage-directquery-connections-to-dataset

**16. Unique names.** The flag `forceUniqueNames` stops a measure from taking the name of any column. This template already asks the same (M006). Only Microsoft's library reference documents it. Example: the same `model.tmdl` as rule 15. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.model.forceuniquenames

**17. Value filter behavior (preview).** For models where filters on two columns of one table must stay apart instead of being merged into the combinations that exist. `independent` keeps them apart; `coalesced` merges them; `automatic` merges today and may change when the preview ends. Set in the model's Properties pane. Stored as `valueFilterBehavior: independent` in `model.tmdl` (level 1606). Example: `preview/ValueFilter.SemanticModel`, built on Microsoft's own scenario. No check. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/value-filter-behavior

**18. Data access options.** Settings of the Power Query engine that Power BI writes on new models. Stored as `dataAccessOptions` with the bare flags `legacyRedirects` and `returnErrorValuesAsNull` one level deeper. Leave the lines as Power BI wrote them; do not add or remove them by hand. Example: `storage/ModelOptions.SemanticModel/definition/model.tmdl`. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/articles/item-management/definitions/semantic-model-definition ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.model.dataaccessoptions

**19. Automatic aggregations.** Training and query coverage are set in the semantic model settings in the service, for DirectQuery models on Premium, Premium Per User or Embedded. Microsoft keeps that setting outside the model, and the tables it makes are managed by the service: never edit them. Not built. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/aggregations-auto ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/aggregations-auto-configure

**20. Unicode character behaviour.** For models that must meet China's GB18030-2022 standard. `codePoints` makes LEN, LEFT, MID, RIGHT, FIND and REPLACE count a character such as an emoji as one; the default `codeUnits` counts it as two. Microsoft sets it with an XMLA command and then a full refresh. Stored as `unicodeCharacterBehavior: codePoints` in `database.tmdl`. Example: `storage/ModelOptions.SemanticModel/definition/database.tmdl`. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/best-practices/dax-unicode-character-behavior

## D. Files and folders of a model folder

**21. `TMDLScripts/` and `DAXQueries/`.** Desktop saves each tab of TMDL view as a `.tmdl` file in `TMDLScripts/`, and each tab of DAX query view as a `.dax` file in `DAXQueries/`; their tab settings sit in `.pbi`. They are scripts, not the model: running one changes the model only when a person applies it in Desktop. Copilot may read them. It does not write or edit them unless the developer asks, and it never treats them as the source of truth; the model is `definition/`. A Git setup started from the workspace leaves TMDL view scripts out. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/projects/projects-dataset ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-tmdl-view ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/dax-query-view

**22. `changedProperty` lines.** Power BI writes them under an object to record that one of its properties was changed (level 1567). This template reads them as marks of a person's change to an object that Power BI keeps in sync. Never write one by hand and never remove one; keep it when you edit the object. Microsoft Learn gives only the library class. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.analysisservices.tabular.changedproperty

**23. `Copilot/` (Prep data for AI, preview).** It holds what the developer sets in Prep data for AI: the AI data schema (`schema.json`: the fields Copilot uses, with visibility and synonyms), AI instructions (`Instructions/`), verified answers (`VerifiedAnswers/`), plus `examplePrompts.json`, `settings.json` and `version.json`. Read only for Copilot: the developer sets all of it in Power BI. Why: Microsoft never says the files are edited by hand, and rule 17 of the file `model-standard.md` beside this one keeps linguistic setup in Power BI. Limits: Q&A is on; in Desktop only Import, DirectQuery and local composite models; instructions are at most 10,000 characters and may not be followed; verified answers do not support Git integration, REST APIs or deployment pipelines, and do not fully respect row-level or object-level security; after a Git deployment the model is refreshed in the service. Schemas: `scripts/schemas/fabric/item/semanticModel/copilot`. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-prepare-data-ai ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-prepare-data-ai-data-schema ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-prepare-data-ai-instructions ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-prepare-data-ai-verified-answers ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/articles/item-management/definitions/semantic-model-definition

**24. Other files.** None is edited by Copilot.
- `.gitignore` (project root): Desktop writes it only when none exists; it keeps `.pbi/localSettings.json` and `.pbi/cache.abf` out of Git. Lines may be added by the developer. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/projects/projects-overview
- `item.metadata.json` and `item.config.json`: the older form of `.platform` (type, display name, description; version and logicalId). A folder has either the pair or `.platform`, never both; a commit replaces the pair. Never change the logicalId or the type. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/cicd/git-integration/source-code-format
- `modelReference.json`: optional; points to a model hosted outside Power BI, with its connection string and type. Source: its schema, `scripts/schemas/fabric/item/semanticModel/modelReference`.
- `.schedules`: Fabric's file of scheduled jobs for an item under Git integration; set in Fabric, not by hand. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/job-scheduler
- `.pbi/unappliedChanges.json`: Power Query edits saved with Apply later. Applying them overwrites the queries in the model, so an edit made outside Desktop to the same queries is lost. Tell the developer when the file exists. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/projects/projects-dataset

**25. Fabric Git integration.** A workspace admin connects a workspace to one branch and one folder, the Git folder setting; items then sync both ways. On every commit Fabric deletes files inside an item folder that are not part of the item, so keep no file of your own inside a model or report folder. For several workspaces Microsoft advises one branch with a Git folder per workspace. This template never connects to a workspace: that is the developer's decision. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/cicd/git-integration/git-get-started ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/cicd/git-integration/git-integration-process ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/understand-best-practices-fabric-cicd

## Not confirmed from Microsoft

- That Power BI Desktop opens a model at compatibility level 1705 (the user-context column needs it in Microsoft's library; Learn's compatibility-level page names 1700 as the latest).
- That Desktop keeps `refreshPolicy` with `mode: hybrid`, a second partition, `dataCoverageDefinition` or `unicodeCharacterBehavior` when it saves a project; Learn sets these through the XMLA endpoint.
- The spelling `nonVisual`: Learn writes `nonvisual`; the shipped example keeps the serializer's spelling.
- How Desktop stores multi-select and Select all of a dynamic M query parameter, and how it stores groups and bins.
- What each file of `Copilot/` holds beyond what its schema shows.
- A Microsoft page that says when Power BI writes `changedProperty`.

Checklist items: 16, 17, 30, 38
